| [NOTE-050](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-050.md) v2 | The relativity of causal knowledge | The paper defines SCMs as functors I → Prob and interventions as natural transformations (which requires invertible mixing functions). It encodes each non-intervened SCM as the convex space Δ(V, Ω) of all probability measures on its endogenous space, and puts these spaces on a graph as stalks of a network sheaf and cosheaf. The restriction maps are interventionally consistent α-abstractions and the extension maps are unspecified affine maps. "Relative causal knowledge" is the image of alternating restriction and extension along a path (Def. 11). The two substantive-looking theorems are either unsound or vacuous. Theorem 1 (every convex combination of a model's interventional measures is a soft-interventional measure of it) rests on a proof step that is false. Theorems 2 and 3 hold for any pushforward map, so interventional consistency does no work in them. There are no results about the sheaf. | Read |
| [NOTE-053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-053.md) v4 | Transfer entropy as a log-likelihood ratio | For a parametric Markov model f(x_t \| x^k_t, y^k_t; θ) of X, the likelihood-ratio estimator T̂ = −(1/(n−k)) log Λ for the null "no dependence on Y's past" converges almost surely to the transfer entropy T_{Y→X} (Theorem 1a). Under the null, 2(n−k)T̂ is asymptotically χ²(d), with d the difference in parameter counts (Theorem 1b). For finite-state chains the ordinary plug-in estimator is exactly this estimator, with d = (a−1)a^k(b^k−1). For a linear Gaussian VAR, T̂ is half the Granger-causality statistic. | Read |

| [NOTE-091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-091.md) v2 | Pernu — Mental causation via neuroprosthetics? | The interventionist/difference-making case for nonreductive mental causation from BCIs (List & Menzies 2009; Menzies 2015; Woodward 2008a,b, 2017) misplaces multiple realisation. Each intention M corresponds to one value of N. So the counterfactual contrast "∼M □→ ∼B true, ∼N □→ ∼B false" fails, and neuroprosthetics supports mental causation only by identifying M with N, not nonreductive physicalism. | Read |
| [NOTE-092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-092.md) v2 | Quillien — Luck and intentional action | Across three Prolific studies (N = 198, 673, 142; Likert 1–7), judgments that "X happened because the agent wanted X" track intentionality judgments under manipulations of luck. | [NOTE-111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-111.md) v2 | Baedke et al. — Unknotting reciprocal causation | The paper gives an epistemic, not a metaphysical, tool for organism–environment reciprocal causation. | [NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md) v3 | Poltorak — Wave-function realism and causal closure | A closure principle has two tacit parameters, its domain and its completeness relation (causal, dynamical or explanatory). The physicalist is left with a dilemma: STC is too narrow, and FPC needs an independent criterion of physicality plus a dynamical-to-causal bridge. | [NOTE-137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-137.md) v2 | Hazelwood — Emerging dilemma for reciprocal causation | Hazelwood defines RC as "the process of natural selection is both a cause and effect of processes such as niche construction" and EC as "natural selection is an emergent causal process". If EC holds, niche construction partly composes selection, so the two fail Woodward's independent-fixability condition and cannot stand in a causal relation. If EC fails, selection is either non-causal (statisticalism) or individual-level, which is incoherent because relative fitness needs a population (Millstein, Sober). EES proponents should drop RC but can keep niche construction as a genuine cause of the evolutionary *product*. | Read |

| [NOTE-1045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1045.md) | Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern — Approximate causal abstraction | Turns τ-abstraction into a graded relation. Probabilistic versions average over contexts and, with an intervention distribution, over the low-level ways of implementing each high-level intervention.
